case_study_md:
# EasyDrive Ecosystem

## Overview

EasyDrive is a connected automotive ecosystem made up of a public vehicle marketplace and a focused financing acquisition product. I owned full-stack delivery across customer journeys, operational tooling, and integrations.

## Business Problem

Vehicle discovery, credit pre-approval, lead delivery, and dealership operations were fragmented. Buyers needed a trustworthy path from browsing to financing, while staff needed structured records instead of manual handoffs.

## Solution

I built EasyDrive Canada for discovery, inventory, accounts, purchase support, and dealer operations, plus EasyDrive Finance for vehicle-first pre-approval and scored lead delivery.

## Key Workflows

Customers browse verified inventory, request financing, manage purchase steps, and move into coordinated follow-up. Teams manage leads, appointments, customers, vendors, inventory, sales, e-signatures, reports, billing, and configuration.

## Architecture and Integrations

Typed React applications use server-side workflows, Supabase services, Stripe, email delivery, Google Sheets and CRM-compatible lead routing, analytics events, and Playwright coverage. The second live product is https://easydrivefinance.ca/.

## Reliability and Security

Sensitive operations remain server-side, validation is shared across boundaries, access is role-scoped, and lead delivery has explicit failure handling.

## Challenges and Trade-offs

The challenge was joining two conversion journeys without coupling releases. I kept product boundaries clear and standardized the acquisition-to-operations handoff.

## Outcome

The result is a live platform spanning acquisition UX, transactional workflows, and operational software—not just a marketing site.

# RewardMe

## Overview

RewardMe is a live local rewards product serving members and participating businesses. I was the sole full-stack developer for the majority of the build and translated the commercial model into a coherent public and operational experience.

## Business Problem

Members needed to understand how they earn and use rewards. Businesses needed a practical way to publish offers, verify eligible activity, and choose participation terms without confusing rewards with advertising.

## Solution

I built distinct member and business journeys connected by clear offer terms, membership tiers, verified purchase activity, and reward balances.

## Key Workflows

Members discover offers, create an account, use QR credentials, and track rewards. Businesses review benefits, apply, publish terms, verify purchases, and work from a dedicated portal.

## Architecture and Integrations

The delivered experience uses role-aware application boundaries, reusable offer and membership rules, QR-assisted identity and purchase flows, localized English, Tagalog, and Spanish content, and auditable records.

## Reliability and Security

Role separation, explicit transaction states, validated offer terms, and traceable verification reduce ambiguity around recording or redeeming value.

## Challenges and Trade-offs

The hardest decision was explaining a novel model without overloading either audience. I separated the journeys and repeated important terms at decision points.

## Outcome

RewardMe is a polished two-sided product with a credible member proposition, concrete business onboarding, and workflows designed for real activity.

# Synergize Business Group

## Overview

Synergize is an invite-only B2B credit network where businesses earn credit from idle capacity and spend it with other members. I delivered the full-stack product from public positioning through private operations.

## Business Problem

A credit network needs more than a directory: membership must be controlled, balances trustworthy, private offers private, and every adjustment operationally explainable.

## Solution

I built invite requests, member access, private offerings, industry discovery, a value calculator, administrative tools, and an auditable credit ledger.

## Key Workflows

Prospects request an invitation; approved members discover businesses and offers and exchange credit. Administrators manage members, offers, balances, and exceptions.

## Architecture and Integrations

The React and TypeScript application uses Supabase and PostgreSQL, serverless endpoints for privileged actions, SQL migrations for business rules, and automated browser coverage.

## Reliability and Security

Role checks protect private surfaces. Credit mutations are atomic, retry-safe, and idempotent so repeated requests cannot apply value twice.

## Challenges and Trade-offs

The challenge was making a financial-like system approachable while preserving strict invariants. I kept member language simple and concentrated complexity in tested server operations.

## Outcome

The live platform turns an unusual commercial model into a credible product with clear acquisition, protected member value, and maintainable operations.

# Innerfire Co.

## Overview

Innerfire Co. is a live premium commerce experience for ceremonial cacao. I connected its product, subscription, educational, and brand-story surfaces into one customer journey.

## Business Problem

Customers had to understand the ritual, sourcing, research, preparation, and subscription value before feeling confident enough to buy.

## Solution

I built a distinctive Shopify experience with a clear value proposition supported by product detail, starter options, bundles, subscriptions, stockists, research, and a transparent founder story.

## Key Workflows

Visitors can understand the category, compare ways to start, browse products, select recurring or one-time purchase, learn preparation, find stockists, and move into checkout.

## Architecture and Integrations

The storefront uses Shopify commerce, reusable responsive content sections, structured merchandising, subscription-aware calls to action, account and cart flows, and search-friendly editorial content.

## Reliability and Security

Commerce, account, and checkout remain on the established Shopify platform while the custom experience focuses on presentation and responsive behavior.

## Challenges and Trade-offs

The trade-off was cinematic storytelling versus fast decisions. I preserved the identity while repeating concrete purchase paths at natural points.

## Outcome

Innerfire presents as a credible premium brand with a memorable visual system and a complete path from explanation to repeat purchase.

# Loyality / Medellin Rewards

## Overview

Loyality is a full-stack rewards foundation delivered publicly through programs including Medellin Rewards. I owned the majority of development across member, business, administrator, platform, deployment, and mobile surfaces.

## Business Problem

A real program must coordinate customer identity, business participation, balances, redemptions, reporting, localization, and support. Ad-hoc points tracking cannot provide the isolation or auditability required for multiple programs.

## Solution

I built a tenant-aware platform and localized Medellin experience with bilingual acquisition, member accounts, business workflows, QR transactions, memberships, gift cards, administrative reporting, and program configuration.

## Key Workflows

Members join, discover businesses, use QR credentials, earn value, and redeem rewards. Businesses manage activity and reports. Administrators control operations without crossing tenant boundaries.

## Architecture and Integrations

The React and TypeScript client uses Supabase, PostgreSQL, server-side services, storage, email, and deployment automation. It ships as a PWA with Capacitor wrappers.

## Reliability and Security

Row-level policies, tenant-scoped services, idempotent redemption, atomic fulfillment, migrations, health checks, and cross-tenant tests protect financial-like records.

## Challenges and Trade-offs

The challenge was growing from one program into a reusable platform without leaking brand, language, data, or permissions. Shared behavior moved into tenant-aware services.

## Outcome

Medellin Rewards is live, and Loyality supports repeatable program delivery with serious operational and security foundations.

# Pokebuddy

## Overview

Pokebuddy is a study assistant that answers Pokémon questions using retrieval-augmented generation rather than model memory alone.

## Problem

Static databases are accurate but cumbersome for exploratory questions, while generic chat systems can invent details and hide sources.

## Solution

I built a React and Django application that retrieves reference documents, reranks candidates, generates a grounded response, and shows citations. It supports stat lookups, fuzzy correction, session memory, and team-building questions.

## Architecture

ChromaDB stores embeddings, Django exposes retrieval and conversation APIs, SQLite persists sessions, and PokeAPI enriches structured results. OpenAI and local Ollama providers share one interface.

## Reliability

Citation cards keep answers verifiable, fallbacks preserve behavior when a model or API is unavailable, and fuzzy matching recovers common input errors.

## Outcome

The project demonstrates an end-to-end RAG workflow with the retrieval, evidence, and failure-handling concerns required for dependable AI features.

# IssuePilot

## Overview

IssuePilot is an archived multi-workspace issue tracking build focused on software and QA teams.

## Problem

Enterprise trackers can be difficult to configure, while simple boards often lack workspace isolation, role controls, reproduction detail, and meaningful analytics.

## Solution

I designed a React and Supabase SaaS with isolated workspaces, projects, memberships, issues, attachments, saved filters, QA fields, a drag-and-drop Kanban board, and analytics.

## Technical Decisions

PostgreSQL row-level security scopes every query to valid membership. Storage policies protect attachments. Enum-backed states keep client and database aligned, while optimistic updates make the board responsive and roll back failed writes.

## Outcome

Although no longer hosted, IssuePilot remains a strong reference for multi-tenant data modeling, authorization, and maintainable feature-based structure.

# AI Tweet Generator

## Overview

This is a configurable AI writing workspace for drafting and comparing social posts.

## Problem

A single text box does not match a real content workflow. Users need reusable prompts, multiple output options, predictable length and tone controls, review context, and provider resilience.

## Solution

I built single, batch, streaming, and vision-assisted modes with twelve categorized templates, tone and creativity controls, character targeting, a realistic preview, history, favorites, and copy or post actions.

## Architecture

Typed adapters normalize Groq, OpenAI, Hugging Face, DeepSeek, and Together AI requests. Custom hooks manage streaming cancellation, while browser APIs handle media previews, clipboard actions, and local persistence.

## Outcome

The application demonstrates product-level AI integration: configurable inputs, provider fallback, responsive feedback, error handling, and review tools around the model response.

# DailyMacros

## Overview

DailyMacros is a live ordering platform where customers build protein shakes with immediate nutrition and price feedback while staff manage the menu and fulfillment.

## Problem

Custom ingredients create combinatorial pricing, unit, allergen, and nutrition rules. Hiding calculations until checkout creates errors and weakens trust.

## Solution

I built an interactive builder that converts ingredient units, updates macros and price in real time, flags allergens, and supports presets and custom orders. QR-linked tracking keeps customers informed.

## Operations

Staff and administrators manage drinks, ingredients, add-ons, pricing modes, order states, labels, and audit records through role-protected tools. Supabase provides authentication, data, and synchronized updates.

## Outcome

The product joins a transparent customer experience with the controls needed to keep a configurable menu accurate and fulfill orders reliably.

# GoDavao

## Overview

GoDavao is a cross-platform rideshare concept designed around transportation patterns in Davao, Philippines.

## Problem

Global ride models do not always cover shared local routes, group flat fares, or hourly Pakyaw rentals. Addresses and preferred driver routes can also be less standardized.

## Solution

I built passenger and driver modes in Flutter with route discovery, booking, ride requests, live status, history, ratings, vehicle management, and multiple ride types.

## Architecture

Supabase provides authentication, PostgreSQL data, and real-time updates. OSRM generates routes, while manual polyline support gives drivers control where automatic routing is not enough. Fare rules account for distance, duration, peak demand, night surcharges, fees, and carpool discounts.

## Outcome

The source demonstrates a localized mobile marketplace with mapping, pricing, live coordination, and safety considerations across both sides of a ride.
